case_title: Selvaraj @ Chinnapaiyan v. State Represented by Inspector of Police
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, was alleged to have caused the death of his 39-day-old daughter. The child was taken to a hospital where she later died. The prosecution claimed the accused strangled the child with a gunny wire and inserted paddy seeds into her mouth. The medical examination did not show signs of strangulation or asphyxia. The autopsy report indicated the child might have died due to sudden death syndrome. Key witnesses, including the mother and maternal relatives of the victim, initially supported the prosecution but later contradicted their statements during cross-examination. The prosecution failed to establish the cause of death as homicidal, and the medical evidence did not confirm the accused's involvement in the child's death.
